pr_title: [browser][wasm] Add support for marshaling Enum through the bindings
pr_body:
Initial support for marshaling Enum types through the bindings.

Closes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/40188

Javascript does not have support for Enum data types and instead ordinarily uses strings to represent property values.  Although, this is not always true as they can be [typed as well](https://javascript.info/dom-attributes-and-properties#dom-properties-are-typed) most property values can be expressed as strings.

An example is the [Color property](https://www.w3schools.com/jsref/prop_style_color.asp).

The marshaling code allows one to set a binding contract through the `Export` Attribute to help facilitate the marshaled values.

```
    public enum ConvertEnum
    {
        Default,
        ToLower,
        ToUpper,
        Numeric
    }
```

example:

```
        public enum StyleColor : uint
        {
           RedNoExport,
            [Export(EnumValue = ConvertEnum.Default)]
            Red = 0xff0000ff,
            [Export(EnumValue = ConvertEnum.Numeric)]
            GreenNumeric = 0x00ff00ff,
            [Export("red", EnumValue = ConvertEnum.ToUpper)]
            RedUpperCase,
            [Export("RED", EnumValue = ConvertEnum.ToLower)]
            RedLowerCase,
            [Export("#ff0000")]
            RedHex
        }
```

- No `Export` attribute.  `RedNoExport ` is marshaled as the string `RedNoExport `
- ConvertEnum.Default uses the Enum value itself.  `Red` is marshaled as the string `Red`
- ConvertEnum.ToLower will convert the enum value to lower case before marshaling the value. `Red` is marshaled as the string `red`.
- ConvertEnum.ToUpper will convert the enum value to upper case before marshaling the value. `Red` is marshaled as the string `RED`.
- ConvertEnum.Numeric will marshal the numeric value instead of the string value.  'GreenNumeric' will be marshaled as 16711935

One can also marshal a set value as well by using the `ContractName` parameter of the `Export` attribute.

```
            [Export("#ff0000")]
            RedHex
```

Will be marshaled as `#ff0000`.

The `Export` attribute also facilitates the marshaling of these values from JS to managed code.

**** Note **** 

Restriction on Enum type of long and ulong exist as JavaScript does not at this time have support for native int64 values.

issue_context.title: [browser][bindings] Enum bindings regression from mono 3.2
issue_context.body: The enum bindings need to be added to the dotnet/runtime

review_comments: Should we check for `value == null` here?

What's the expected behavior if we have:

```
{
             Blue
             [EnumExport("RedExport")]
             Red = 0xff0000ff
}
```

.. and the string to be marshaled is `"Red"`? Tests needed for this too.

Please add tests where
	- multiple Export attributes exist
	- Export with the same value is used for multiple enum values
	- values don't match to any of enum values

Tests for this case, like 
1. when value is an object/array being passed from JS, dunno if it can get to this point or not.
2. value is a number that is not a valid enum value

Should this assert, or return null, or exception? Line 420 has the same check, but returns null if it isn't true.
Tests for this too.

What is the expected behavior if we have:

```
             RedNoExport = 3,

             [EnumExport("RedNoExport")]
             Red = 0xff0000ff,
             ...
```

What about:
```
             [EnumExport("Green")]
             RedNoExport,

             [EnumExport("Green")]
             Red = 0xff0000ff,
```

We should add tests for these too, whatever the behavior.
should this just return null, if `obj == null`?

Would it be useful to have tests for enums being returned from methods/functions?
How about a test for array of enums being marshaled?

Array of enums is not supported right now nor native arrays in general.  They all use a JavaScript object to marshal back and forth.  We can set up a PR for an enhancement to support native arrays but I have not found any examples that actually use an array of enums.  What could be done is create a JavaScript.Array object and fill it out with what is needed to be passed.
nit: instead of parsing we could do `return (Enum)fi.GetValue(null);`
This results in Converting null literal or possible null value to non-nullable type.
Is the marshaling expected to be case-sensitive? We should tests for that in either case.
Check for null, or empty string? and add a test.
Is this needed? Is `[EnumExport] Red,` a valid case? If so, we should add a test for that too.
It is now.  Added support in recent commits.
